title: C3075 — Front seat height adjustment motor RH connector
introduction:
I use the function wording here to keep rear seat-height adjustment distinct from other seat movements. The assigned connections are labelled for lowering and raising the rear of the passenger seat. That distinction is useful: a seat switch can offer a small furniture ballet, and this map identifies only the movements named in its rows.

Start with the connector identity table, compare the face drawing’s housing features, then carry a cavity label into the matching table row. Read across for the circuit identification, wire information, function and terminal reference. The shaded positions correspond to unused rows; available housing space and assigned wiring are different things.

The pigtail table is a separate parts record. This reading guide does not define the physical viewing side, Size code or gauge convention, and it provides no access, probing, motor-test or replacement method. Keep the printed data intact; it does not establish electrical condition or authorize wire substitution.

edits.why: I use the upper housing detail and the step at the drawing’s lower right as landmarks. The outlined cavity positions appear on the left and the shaded positions on the right. This describes the supplied face drawing; it does not establish the connector’s installed orientation or a latch-release movement.

The Cavity column connects each drawing label to its electrical assignment. Read the full function wording so rear-height down and rear-height up remain distinct from other possible seat movements. The shaded positions agree with rows marked unused. Direction labels identify the assigned connections without specifying motor polarity, test voltage or an energizing procedure.

I keep the pigtail assembly’s service-part and shell record separate from the individual terminal records in the assignment table. The pigtail’s cavity count describes its housing capacity, while the assignment rows show which positions this application uses. Its gauge entry does not explain how to adapt it to the circuit wiring or teach a replacement.
